question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(r)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}15{r}^{3}-50{r}^{2} & =-40r \\ 15{r}^{3}-50{r}^{2}+40r & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $5r.$ We can factor out the $5r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}15{r}^{3}-50{r}^{2}+40r & =0 \\ 5r(3{r}^{2}-10r+8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $3{r}^{2}-10r+8$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5r(3{r}^{2}-10r+8) & =0 \\ 5r(3r-4)(r-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $r=0,$ $r=\frac{4}{3},$ and $r=2.$
